newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latam stocks seen rising as U.S. outlook improves.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen rising as U.S. outlook improves.

text.p: Latin American stocks were mostly expected to rise this week, bouyed by isolated in-country developments that investors viewed as positive as well as by a healthy kick-off to the week on Wall Street.
"It has to be a week of gains; we think the Mexican market could go up 2.5 percent," said one Mexico City-based stocks trader. "The Dow is so strong it could hit record levels."
That optimism jarred with a sluggish performance on the Bolsa on Monday, but volume was wafer-thin. Traders expected the market to be bouyed by August inflation data due out later Monday.
One trader said the market's drop early Monday was partly because foreign investors preferred to stay in U.S. stocks.
Also, Lehman Brothers cut Telmex's 1997 earnings estimate to $3.35 from $3.76 per ADS.
Mexico's IPC index closed on Friday at 3,340.93.

Argentine stocks were expected to seesaw over the next few days and close the week more or less flat after their recent strong recovery, dealers said. "The focus will be on Congress Wednesday, when the government's tax package may finally come up for debate, and on any new labor reform announcements," said Emilio Alessandro of broker Alessandro.
The tax package was unveiled four weeks ago by Economy Minister Roque Fernndez, who took office July 29, replacing Domingo Cavallo.

The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index jumped 4.4 percent last week to close Friday at 532.26 and stand at its highest level since August 9. Technical analysts forecast the MerVal would rub up against resistance at 540 points but doubted it could fall back below 530 in the near-term.
The bolsa was also likely to stay under the influence of Wall Street this week, although if volumes remained healthy it could keep an independent strong undertone, dealers said.
After recovering late last week, Chilean stocks could be poised for modest gains as local institutional investors including pension funds return to the market, brokers said.
"The market is looking firmer, more on the basis of local fund buying than foreign demand," said one broker.

Others cautioned that last week's gains were due largely to rumors and unconfirmed news reports about big mergers and acquisitions in the electrical sector. The market could lose steam if it didn't start receiving some real news either confirming or denying the rumors, brokers said.
Attention last week centered on reports, denied by the Chilean party, that Spanish electricity firm Endesa was eyeing a large stake in Chilean electric generator Endesa.
Volume was expected to be low during a short trading week in Chile. Wednesday is a national holiday to commemorate the anniversary of the 1973 coup.
The blue-chip IPSA index ended Friday at 97.72 points, up 1.7 percent for the week.
Caracas stocks, meanwhile, were seen rebounding gently after steady falls last week.
The government's efforts to put privatization hiccups behind encouraged investors that Venezuela remains committed to reform and spurred some cautious buying late last week.
Brokers have noted particular interest in issuers with American Depository Receipts.
Stock prices which had fallen for six consecutive sessions edged up Friday, with the market's 19-share index ending the week off just 0.28 percent at 4,588.43.
-- Henry Tricks, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9560
